summary: Marco Casario examines the macroeconomic consequences of Donald Trump's proposed reciprocal tariffs targeting the 'Dirty 15' trade partners. He explains that while tariffs initially push up consumer prices, their lasting impact is demand destruction and economic stagnation rather than persistent inflation. Market reactions reflect these growth concerns, highlighted by falling bond yields, surging gold prices, and equity indices testing recent lows. Casario also demonstrates tactical hedging methods and explains how to screen for defensive momentum assets during market downturns.
tone_evidence: Casario repeatedly warns that VIX levels above 20 trigger irrational market behavior and cautions that tariffs will depress economic growth.

key_points.point: Tariffs act as an indirect regressive tax paid by domestic importers and passed to consumers, ultimately curbing aggregate demand.
Long-term bond yields are falling and gold is climbing because investors are pricing in economic slowdown and stagnation rather than runaway inflation.
Major investment banks forecast reciprocal tariffs could shave over one percentage point off annual US GDP growth.
A drop in S&P 500 towards the 5,100-5,338 range would represent a typical harmonic extension and retest of key multi-month support.
Recession is not yet confirmed by hard macroeconomic figures, although soft sentiment surveys show clear deterioration.

predictions: If the S&P 500 completes a second downward leg, it could reach the 5,100 to 5,338 Fibonacci extension zone.
Equity market volatility is set to remain elevated as the VIX trades above the critical 20 threshold.
catalysts: Implementation of Trump's reciprocal tariffs announced for April 2nd
US Non-Farm Payrolls report scheduled for Friday
title: 🔴I Mercati TREMANO in vista dei Dazi Reciproci
author: Marco Casario
